correctness.rationale: For every integer 1<=k<ell, the two divisor-sum identities show fixed_divisor(a^ell-a^k) divides every c_{k,ell}(n). Conversely, if p^e divides every coefficient, c_{k,ell}(p^2)=(p^k-p^ell)(1-p^{k+ell}) forces e<=k. For any p-coprime u, multiplying by p^a with ak>=e eliminates the n^k,n^ell terms modulo p^e; multiplicativity and sigma_k(p^a)=1 mod p give sigma_k(u)=sigma_ell(u) mod p^e. Möbius inversion on p-coprime divisors gives u^k=u^ell mod p^e, and p-multiples vanish because e<=k. Hence the two gcds agree exactly. The largest p^e for which all units have t-th power 1 is determined by Carmichael lambda(p^e); taking min with k yields the asserted odd-prime and 2-adic formulas including k=1 and t odd. Independently computed gcd of coefficients n=2..120 for (k,ell)=(1,2),(1,3),(2,5),(3,7),(4,10),(6,9), obtaining 2,6,2,120,504,2; finite sample corroborates, not proves, the universal identity.
